document.abstract: An explosive sensitivity test has been devised wherein specimens of explosives of the order of a pound in weight are squeezed between an explosive-driven plate and a massive anvil. By using the Beckman & Whitley Model 189 Framing Camera, it is possible to observe the movement of the driving plate, the propagation of the nonreactive shock in the explosive sample, the deformation of the explosive as a result of its being squeezed, and in some cases the onset and propagation of an explosive reaction. Conditions within the explosive, such as pressure, density change and particle velocity, are readily computed from the photographs.
